title: Publish chain: push scenarios → JFRED → jfredToolsPlugin, verify clean-room + marketplace, sync wrapper clone
description:
Consolidated go-public checklist from four implementation-notes files:
(1) User must push the scenarios repo (1 unpushed commit 075ef56 "added S86, updated S41") BEFORE JFRED is pushed — JFRED's pin was fetched from the local clone and dangles for cloners until then.
(2) JFRED is staged but uncommitted; first commit + push still needs the privacy gate re-run at push time. Commit ordering: commit inside jfred/jfredToolsPlugin first, push, then re-stage the gitlink in JFRED (it currently records the license-only commit 70ad1b6), commit JFRED, then RevEng.
(3) Consider switching the GitHub default branch for matkatmusic/jfred from master (empty initial commit — a plain git clone gets an empty tool) to develop: `gh repo edit matkatmusic/jfred --default-branch develop`.
(4) After pushing jfredToolsPlugin to https://github.com/matkatmusic/jfredToolsPlugin, verify the install flow with a real `claude plugin marketplace add matkatmusic/jfredToolsPlugin` + `claude plugin install`, then decide whether the zshrc --plugin-dir wrapper (task 108's interim enablement) should be retired.
(5) ~/Programming/jfredToolsPlugin (the clone the claude() wrapper actually loads) does NOT yet have the two new scenario skills — pull/push the canonical $REVENG/jfred/jfredToolsPlugin changes into it after committing, or /impl-scenario and /plan-scenario won't resolve at the next launch (their RevEng copies are now archived).
(6) Deferred verifications left for the user from task 111: RevEng `npm test` (5 task-workflow tests + 2 python tests remain), `npm run typecheck`, clean-room `npm test`, and the interactive /run-scenario check under `command claude`.

title: Investigate: agent edit near JSONL line 77 has no timeline entry — pre-baseline trim drops the edit's event (baseline-demo)
description: In baseline-demo, the agent message at JSONL line 77 ('added least_valuable(store) ...') has no matching tool-result/edit entry in the timeline, so the JSONL line where the edit occurred can't be navigated to from the timeline. Confirmed mechanism candidate: when pre-baseline reconstruction is declined, seedBaseCommitBeacon (jfred/src/reconstruction_base_commit.ts:132) drops every FileEvent at-or-before the beacon insertion point ('dropped N superseded pre-baseline event(s)') — the edit's WriteEvent never survives, so no revision, no fileChanges chip, no timeline entry; the git-derived baseline synthetic turn (recordGitBaselineSnapshot, jfred/webapp/views/timeline-nodes.ts:69) absorbs only the gitBase snapshot, it does not literally merge the edit. Verify against the baseline-demo session (was preBaseline declined? does the entry appear when accepted?), then decide the fix: even when trimmed, the turn should probably still be navigable to its JSONL line even if its file event is superseded.

title: Prev/Next buttons should disable at the ends instead of clamping silently
description: Prev/Next enablement should reflect whether there is anywhere to jump: at line 0, [◀ Prev] must be disabled; at the last line (index length-1), [Next ▶] must be disabled. Today the inspector's record stepper (buildInspectorNavigationRow, jfred/webapp/inspector.ts:121) keeps both buttons enabled and clamps out-of-range steps to a no-op. Fix: set button.disabled on render from the clamped index (prev: index === 0; next: index === rawLines.length - 1). Apply the same rule to the OTHER prev/next pair — the timeline header's #files-prev/#files-next (wireFileNavButtons, jfred/webapp/views/timeline-render-selection.ts:91): disable when findAdjacentFileTouchedIndex (timeline-sessions.ts:92) returns no hit in that direction (also covers the zero-file-touching-rows case). Pairs with task 131 (what the header buttons step over) — if 131 changes the step granularity, the enablement predicate follows whatever collection it lands on.

title: Script-run row: 'modified 6 files' pill counts paths, not files (rename pairs double-counted)
description: In s85-git-commit-csv-and-move-scripts (timeline row for JSONL line 103), the pill says 'modified 6 file(s)' but only 3 files were modified — the script's shutil.move() calls operate on filename PAIRS, and the sandbox reports both the deleted source and the created destination as changed paths. Render site: timeline-render-rows.ts:215 — `modified ${node.scriptRun.changedPaths.length} file(s)` (task-67 badge); changedPaths is the sandbox's changed-path list. Fix: collapse rename pairs when counting (a delete whose content reappears at a created path = one move), or reword the badge to what it truly counts (e.g. 'touched 6 path(s)'). Prefer collapsing — 'modified 3 files' matches what the user sees in the diff pane.

title: Script-run detail pane: no per-file view of the run's changes (unlike rev-card rows)
description: Selecting a script-run timeline row (e.g. s85 line 103) shows the executed script in the left column and one aggregate before/after of the whole run in the right column (task-67 mode, timeline-render-selection.ts:59) — there is no easy way to see the changes made to an INDIVIDUAL file, like rev-card rows give. Add per-file selection to the script-run detail pane: a file list (the run's changedPaths, rename pairs collapsed per task 143) where clicking a file shows just that file's before/after diff — reuse the existing rev-card diff machinery (details-revision-view.ts / details-diff.ts) rather than building a new diff renderer.

title: Investigate: s85 script renames missing from the Files nav ('core_one.py <- one.py (renamed)' badge absent)
description: In s85-git-commit-csv-and-move-scripts, files renamed by the script (one.py -> core_one.py etc. via shutil.move) do not show the rename representation in the Files nav column that other projects get (rename badge: renameBadgeLabel stamped by applyRenameBadgeLabels, jfred/webapp/views/timeline-file-tree.ts:45, fed by each history revision's rename?.from — see also renamedFrom in details.ts:56). Likely engine-side: the file tree only shows a badge when the file's history contains a rename REVISION; s85's evidence flows through beaconlessScriptExecutions + the git-commit BLOB channel (reconstruction_git_evidence.ts, placeGitCommitEvidence — see s85 ground truth), which may seed the renamed file's history at its final path with no rename revision. CHECK FIRST (known s85 HAZARD): the s85 repo is resolved via the recorded TEMP cwd (/var/folders/.../run-scenario.*) — if that tmpdir was cleaned, s85 reconstruction regresses wholesale and this symptom (plus task 146) may just be that regression, not a new gap. Run the CLI sweep on s85 before touching the webapp.

title: Investigate: two.py absent from the Files nav in s85 (write at L48 confirmed in transcript)
description: In s85-git-commit-csv-and-move-scripts, two.py never appears in the Files nav: JSONL L48 indicates the write happened, L41 is the tool result, L37 contains two.py's contents — yet no file entry renders. Could be a reconstruction gap (no history built for two.py), a timeline-rendering gap, a rev-card gap, or a Files-nav gap; needs narrowing. Triage order: (1) the known s85 tmpdir HAZARD — reconstruction resolves the repo via the recorded TEMP cwd, and a cleaned /var/folders/.../run-scenario.* tmpdir regresses s85 (same check as task 145; do it once for both); (2) does the wire document contain a history for two.py at all (hit /api/document and grep — engine gap if absent); (3) if present, walk webapp/views/timeline-file-tree.ts / details.ts to find where the entry drops out (rendering gap). File the concrete fix as a follow-up once attributed.

title: Details pane: pin the inspector nav row (prev/next/hook/result/format buttons) above the scrollable JSON
description: The JSON inspector's header row — [◀ Prev] [Next ▶] / go to preToolUse hook / go to tool result / show as formatted text — scrolls away with the record content in the details pane's right column; it should stay always visible. The row is built by buildInspectorNavigationRow (jfred/webapp/inspector.ts:121) and appended into the same scrollable container as the JSON body (#details-right / .inspector-json, markup in jfred/webapp/index.html ~:44-60). Fix is layout-only: keep the nav row a non-scrolling sibling of the scroll container (or position: sticky; top: 0 with an opaque background inside it) — note #details-right already has a fixed #details-right-header (JSON label + find widget), so the cleanest shape is nav row joining that fixed header region rather than a second sticky layer.

title: Filter/find by conversation name in multi-JSONL projects (session custom titles)
description: Add a way to filter or find conversations by their user-given name in multi-JSONL projects. Motivating use case: locate the 'tackle 121' conversation in the RevEng projects dir to inspect the tool-result JSON from the agent's close-tasks 121 invocation. The data plumbing ALREADY exists end-to-end: custom-title records ({type:'custom-title', customTitle, sessionId}) are parsed into document.sessionTitles (findSessionTitles, jfred/src/reconstruction_json.ts:131/:241; wire field :149) and the webapp reads them (timeline-types.ts:92; session-header rows + timeline-labels.ts / timeline-render-row-cells.ts consumers). Behavior is UNDECIDED — candidate shapes, cheapest first: (1) include session titles in the existing task-127 timeline search index so typing 'tackle 121' jumps to that session's header row (zero new UI); (2) a session dropdown in the timeline header listing sessionTitles, jump-to-session-header on pick; (3) a filter chip that hides rows whose node.sessionId belongs to non-matching sessions (nodes already carry sessionId). Note the original 'chip for JSONL lines that have customTitle' framing would only match the title records themselves — the useful unit is the SESSION the title names, so filter/jump by sessionId. Decide the shape when picking this up; (1) likely satisfies the motivating search on its own.

title: Progress UI goes silent for minutes inside 'Phase 4 of 6' on large real sessions
description: Loading the real RevEng project (#/project/-Users-matkatmusicllc-Desktop-claude-code-src-RevEng/timeline) sat in 'Phase 4 of 6' for 500+ seconds with the progress line frozen at '451/451 reconstructing <target>' — the counter reaches N/N and then nothing updates while the long tail runs. Emitter: reportReconstructionProgress fires once per target BEFORE its reconstructFileOver call (jfred/src/reconstruction_renderable.ts:44), so the last label sticks while the final target (and any per-target inner work — replay, sandbox script executions via executeRunOnce) grinds silently; later same-phase stages may emit nothing at all. Fix: finer-grained progress inside the silent stretch — per-target inner-stage labels (e.g. 'reconstructing <target> — replaying run k/n') and/or a heartbeat ('still reconstructing <target>, Ns') so the console visibly advances; audit which Phase-4 stages emit no reportReconstructionProgress at all and give each at least one label. Reproduce with the real ~/.claude/projects RevEng dir (451 targets).

title: Bogus reconstruction targets from Bash command text ('x.taskNumber).join(',')…' reconstructed as a file)
description: During the task-149 stall the progress line read: reconstructing x.taskNumber).join(','))" — i.e. a FRAGMENT OF A BASH COMMAND (a node -e one-liner from a session transcript) became a reconstruction target 'path'. Likely source: discoverScriptCreatedPaths (called in buildRenderableFiles, jfred/src/reconstruction_renderable.ts:36) or the script-run extraction mining paths out of arbitrary Bash command text and admitting garbage tokens as script-created files. On a real messy session this inflates the target list (451 targets for RevEng) and burns reconstruction time on nonsense — possibly the bulk of the 500+ second Phase-4 stall, so fix this BEFORE tuning task-149's progress cosmetics. Fix direction: tighten path candidate validation (must look like a path: no quotes/parens/JS punctuation, plausible separator/extension, or verify existence in evidence channels) at the discovery site, not per caller.

title: Pre-baseline 'No' answer: extend the skip into the script-execution stages
description: Choosing "No" in the pre-baseline reconstruction question still runs the script-execution stages over pre-baseline records — the task-56 text granted "may skip", so only the per-target replay is trimmed today. Extend the skip into the script stage if pre-baseline script runs ever cost noticeable time.

title: Pre-baseline consent: add a 're-ask' control on the timeline header
description: There is no UI to revisit a stored pre-baseline answer short of a new tab / server relaunch (exactly the consent dialog's existing limitation — the answer is stored under a `baseline:` sessionStorage key). Add a "re-ask" control on the timeline header that clears the stored answer and re-poses the pre-baseline question.
